claims.text: High configurational entropy stabilizes the CsCl-type crystal structure of HEA tellurides under high pressure.
High configurational entropy preserves electron–phonon coupling under pressure.
Preservation of electron–phonon coupling maintains a nearly constant superconducting transition temperature.
AgInSnPbBiTe5 is an HEA-type metal telluride with high configurational entropy at the metal site.
AgPbBiTe3 is a middle-entropy telluride, while PbTe is a conventional reference system.
The three material classes can be compared under identical pressures from approximately 13 to 35 GPa.
Configurational entropy governs atomic-site disorder in the metal sublattice.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the electronic environment and lattice structure under pressure.
High configurational entropy reduces pressure-induced band-structure changes and phonon softening.
Middle-entropy and conventional tellurides have less robust electron–phonon interactions under pressure because they contain fewer metal components.
The pressure robustness of superconductivity is linked to configurational entropy of mixing at the metal site.
The superconducting transition temperature of HEA-type AgInSnPbBiTe5 is almost pressure-independent from 13.0 to 35.1 GPa.
The superconducting transition temperature of PbTe decreases with pressure in its high-pressure CsCl-type phase.
AgPbBiTe3 will exhibit pressure dependence of Tc intermediate between AgInSnPbBiTe5 and PbTe.
All three telluride systems are superconducting under high pressure when they have the CsCl-type structure.
The proposed entropy-dependent mechanism applies only while the CsCl-type structure remains stable, and may fail after a phase transition or structural instability.
Local bonding effects may contribute to the pressure dependence of Tc in addition to configurational entropy.
A pressure-induced Tc decrease in the HEA comparable to PbTe, or indistinguishable Tc-pressure behavior across all three systems, would falsify the proposed entropy-based explanation.

contradictions.description: The conditions require constant temperature during measurement, but determining Tc by resistivity or magnetic susceptibility ordinarily requires a temperature sweep; the intended temperature-control protocol is therefore internally unclear.
